fixes.explanation: A king doesn't come into this verse, friend. Verse 18 gives the work to the judges, and it says they shall investigate thoroughly. Nobody gets to just announce a verdict. The judges have to dig into the case first.

Grateful is a nice thought, friend, but the verse says something else. Verse 20 says the rest of the people will hear and be afraid. The people hear about it, and fear is what follows. Nobody in that verse is sending a thank-you card.

Twelve is a big number, friend, but the text says three. Israel is to set apart three cities within the land the LORD is giving them to possess. Verse 3 adds that they are to build roads and divide the land into three regions. Three cities, three regions, and the count stays small.

Revenge is a different story, friend. The man in verse 4 killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him. The passage does turn to a different man in verse 11, one who hates his neighbor, lies in wait, attacks him and kills him. Keep the two men apart in your head and the whole passage gets easier.

True, baker. Verse 9 says that if the LORD gives Israel all the land He promised, and if they carefully keep all these commandments, loving the LORD their God and walking in His ways at all times, then they are to add three more cities to these three. So there are conditions, and the land is only one of them. That makes six cities in all.

Not quite, friend. Verse 9 says that if the LORD gives Israel all the land He promised, and if they carefully keep all these commandments, loving the LORD their God and walking in His ways at all times, then they are to add three more cities to these three. So the answer is True.

That's it, baker. Verse 12 says the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die. Verse 11 describes this man as one who hates his neighbor, lies in wait, attacks him and kills him. So the city doesn't shelter him. The refuge in verses 4 to 6 was for the man who killed accidentally.

Priests do show up later, friend, in verse 17, where both parties in a false witness case stand before the priests and judges. That's a different situation. In verse 12 the elders must send for the man, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die. Same chapter, different case.

Move, baker. Verse 14 says, "You must not move your neighbor’s boundary marker…" Those markers were set up by their ancestors to mark the inheritance. I think it's like nudging the property line over a little at night and hoping nobody checks. Nobody should get away with that, and the verse says don't.
